simple.meaning: בֵּנַיִם (bênayim) is a Hebrew word meaning “a double interval , i.e. the space between two armies.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: בֵּנַיִם (H1143) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at 1 Samuel 17:4, with occurrences in 1 Samuel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to בֵּנַיִם (H1143) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in בֵּנַיִם (H1143) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: בֵּנַיִם (bênayim) / H1143 is traced through 1 Samuel 17:4, 1 Samuel 17:23 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

occurrences.englishText: A champion out of the camp of the Philistines named Goliath, of Gath, whose height was six cubits and a span* A cubit is the length from the tip of the middle finger to the elbow on a man’s arm, or about 18 inches or 46 centimeters. A span is the length from the tip of a man’s thumb to the tip of his little finger when his hand is stretched out (about half a cubit, or 9 inches, or 22.8 cm.) Therefore, Goliath was about 9 feet and 9 inches or 2.97 meters tall. went out.
As he talked with them, behold, the champion, the Philistine of Gath, Goliath by name, came up out of the ranks of the Philistines, and said the same words; and David heard them.
